summary.oneLiner: India's largest pure-play C&I (commercial & industrial) renewable energy company and net-zero partner of choice for corporate India.
summary.business: CleanMax develops, builds, owns and operates renewable energy power projects (wind-solar hybrid, large-scale solar, rooftop/onsite solar, STU & CTU grid-connected plants) and sells the power under long-term PPAs to commercial and industrial customers, complemented by RE services such as energy storage (BESS), asset management and carbon/I-REC solutions. Customers span data centres and AI infrastructure, technology, manufacturing, steel, cement, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, real estate and global capability centres across India and select international markets.

currentContext.strengths: Scale leadership: 3.1 GW operational and 5.7 GW total contracted RE power-sales portfolio as India's largest C&I renewable player|Deep repeat-customer trust: ~74% of FY26 new contracted volumes came from existing clients|High-quality, long-duration contracted revenue: average PPA tenor of ~23 years across 1,280+ PPAs|High-credit-quality counterparty base: over 95%/~82% of customers rated A- and above or AA/AAA-rated / MNC subsidiaries|Early and deepening leadership in the Data Centre/AI demand segment, now ~42% of contracted capacity, up from ~254 MW to 2,380 MW in two years|Integrated, end-to-end execution platform (development to operations) enabling large annual capacity commissioning (~1.4 GW in FY26)
currentContext.strategies: Be the long-term net-zero energy partner for corporate India, anchoring growth in long-term PPAs (average tenor ~23 years) with high-quality counterparties rather than one-off sales.|Deepen leadership in the Data Centre/AI demand segment, which management identifies as the defining infrastructure story of the decade.|Grow as a disciplined, listed public company focused on assets designed to compound over time, leveraging the IPO for deeper governance and capital to build ahead of demand.|Expand CTU-connected portfolio and pioneer Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to address evolving regulatory landscapes and capture peak-hour premiums.|Maintain capital-efficient growth underpinned by disciplined capital allocation and a high-quality, resilient customer portfolio.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a record commissioning year, with ~1.4 GW of new RE power-sales capacity commissioned, including the company's first 525 MWp CTU-connected project in Bikaner, Rajasthan. For FY27, management targets a minimum of 1.5 GW of new commissioned capacity (described as a floor, not a ceiling), backed by over 2.6 GW already contracted and under execution. The company is expanding its CTU-connected portfolio, including the 529 MW Koppal hybrid plant, and is pioneering Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to address evolving regulatory landscapes and capture peak-hour premiums. Over 90% of the FY27 construction pipeline has reportedly been secured (land acquisition) in advance to mitigate execution bottlenecks.
currentContext.mdna: AI, cloud and hyperscale data centres are driving an unprecedented surge in demand for clean, round-the-clock power, positioning CleanMax at the centre of this shift.|Renewables accounted for the largest share of incremental global energy demand growth in 2025 for the first time, with low-emissions sources meeting nearly 60% of the increase in global energy needs.|India added a record 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity in FY26, the highest annual addition in its history, with renewable generation (excluding large hydro) growing 21.1% YoY.|Policy tailwinds support sector growth: GST on renewable energy devices cut from 12% to 5% (Sept 2025), PLI-driven domestic module manufacturing capacity reaching ~172 GW, and completion of Green Energy Corridor Phase-I facilitating power evacuation.|The Commercial & Industrial (C&I) segment has become a dominant force in the wind sector, contributing 75% of new wind capacity additions industry-wide.|Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are emerging as the fastest-growing power technology globally, supported by new tax exemptions in India, positioning storage as a key emerging growth vector.|5.7 GW of total contracted RE power sales capacity as of 31 March 2026, comprising 3.1 GW operational and 2.6 GW contracted and under execution.|1,280+ Power Purchase Agreements in place across the customer base.

risks.risk: Input cost, labour and interest-rate volatility
risks.note: Management explicitly flags fluctuations in raw material prices, labour costs and interest rates among the business and operational risks it is exposed to.

Flagged as a risk in the MD&A; the company also operates cross-border (Dubai, Bahrain, Thailand, Saudi Arabia) with at least one overseas subsidiary reporting in AED, creating currency translation/transaction exposure.
MD&A explicitly names supplier-related challenges and project execution risks as ongoing exposures for a business that must commission gigawatt-scale capacity annually.
Company flags changes in the regulatory environment as a risk factor, relevant given renewable power's dependence on state/central RE policy, grid connectivity and tariff regulation.
Company identifies land-acquisition as a risk to its construction pipeline, stating it has secured over 90% of the FY27 pipeline in advance specifically to neutralise this risk.

risks.risk: Customer/segment concentration in Data Centre & AI
risks.note: ~42% of contracted RE power-sales capacity is concentrated in the Data Centre/AI customer segment, up nearly tenfold in two years, making a large and growing share of the book dependent on a single demand vertical.

one-line thesis: CleanMax scaled operational capacity to 3.1GW (+1.4GW YoY) with 42% of contracted portfolio now tied to Data & AI, driving 28% EBITDA growth and margin expansion; key risks include CTU curtailment in Rajasthan and upcoming ALCM tariffs, but strong client retention (74%) and diversified STU exposure mitigate downside.
financial scorecard: revenue: +28% YoY; EBITDA: +28% YoY to INR1,295cr (margin: 83.5% for PPA, 19.6% for services); PAT (rptd): +4.4x to INR86cr; PAT (normalized): not disclosed; order book: 2,600MW contracted but uncommissioned; net debt: INR9,600cr (net debt/EBITDA: ~4.3x; target 5-5.5x) - one-off: INR414cr pre-tax cash flow hedge gain (zero P&L impact); accounting distortion: negative minority interest due to young asset fleet (PAT negative in early years)
guidance: revenue growth: no guidance; margin: no guidance; order inflow: minimum 1,500MW RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; capex/commissioning: 1,500MW+ new capacity planned; CTU project (530MW) under construction in Karnataka; no battery storage scaling yet
order book & pipeline: 2,600MW contracted but uncommissioned (as of 31-Mar-26); 1,500MW+ expected to be added in FY27; 530MW CTU (wind-heavy) under construction in Karnataka; 1,400MW added in FY26
segment / subsidiary detail: RE Power Sales: 3,100MW operational, 2,600MW contracted; EBITDA margin 83.5% (up from 82%); gross margin stable at 92-93%; RE Services: 555MW operational, 215MW under construction; EBITDA margin 19.6% (up from 14.4%); 74% of new contracts from existing clients
growth verticals / optionality: Data & AI demand (42% of contracted capacity, up from 14% in 2024); expansion into new states (Rajasthan, Andhra, Uttarakhand); potential BESS integration (currently 5-7MW); strategic JVs with Apple, Iron Mountain, STT Data; global big tech partnerships (Meta, Google, Amazon)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expansion driven by SG&A compression (from 18% to 9% of revenue) due to scale; gross margins stable; cost of financing reduced from 9.2% to 8.5% YoY; 40% of debt fixed-rate; ALCM tariff impact expected to be passed to customers via higher tariffs, no margin compression expected
capex / expansion: INR9,600cr net debt reflects capex for 1,400MW FY26 addition; FY27 capex aligned with 1,500MW+ new capacity target; no BESS capex material yet; capital work-in-progress rising with new projects
capital allocation: Debt reduction target: net debt/EBITDA <5.5x; dividend policy: not disclosed; equity raised via IPO; JVs with Apple (INR104cr equity for 49% in 150MW projects); no buybacks or M&A mentioned
risks & watch-items: CTU grid backdown in Rajasthan (13% of run-rate EBITDA exposed; risk up to 6.5% EBITDA if 50% curtailment for full year); DSM regulation uncertainty (sub-judice, impact assessment pending); module cost inflation from ALCM (June 2026); BESS adoption delay; interest rate volatility
management quality / tone: Confident, data-driven, and disciplined; emphasized execution excellence (100% budget adherence), diversification, and client retention; transparent on risks (curtailment, DSM); no financial guidance given but clear capacity targets; tone reflects leadership in C&I renewables
non-obvious takeaways: Run-rate EBITDA (INR1,870cr) is 1.1x reported EBITDA; 99.24% grid uptime indicates near-zero curtailment in STU projects; negative minority interest is accounting artifact of young assets (PAT negative in first 4-5 years); 82% of volume from AA/AAA/MNC clients; 23-year PPA tenor exceeds utility contracts; Apple JV is financial investment, not offtake

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
